threads.body: `InferenceInvocation(...)` is still the constructor being called here, so after `__new__` returns a `SuppressedInferenceInvocation` instance, Python invokes `InferenceInvocation.__init__` (the initializer for the class being constructed), not the subclass initializer below. That runs `GenAIInvocation.__init__`, creates and attaches a second real span, and never initializes the suppression state; nested calls therefore are not deduplicated and the assertions in `test_context.py` for shared spans will fail. Select the concrete class before construction (or explicitly delegate to the suppressed initializer from the base initializer) instead of relying on `__new__` redirection.

threads.body:
Skipping the entire `_process_chunk` hook for a suppressed invocation drops response metadata as well as content. For example, the OpenAI chat hook extracts the response model and token usage in `_process_chunk`, and its stream-end hook copies those buffers to the invocation; when the higher-level instrumentation does not wrap the stream, the root context therefore receives no response model or usage. Suppress only content accumulation (or add a metadata-only hook), not the whole chunk processor.

This issue also appears on line 372 of the same file.

threads.body: The suppressed invocation captures the parent context in `self._span_context`, but publication reads only the context that happens to be current when `stop()`/`fail()` runs. If a caller starts the nested operation in one task/context and finishes it in another (a valid pattern for async streams or deferred completion), `ctx_data` is `None` and all downstream attributes are lost. Read the captured invocation context here, as the non-suppressed implementation does.

Inner wins here: if the outer sets `conversation_id` after start (or relies on the ambient one), the inner's published value fills `data.conversation_id` and overrides it. A later `invocation.conversation_id = ...` is also ignored when one was passed at construction.

```suggestion
                self.conversation_id or self.data.conversation_id,
```

The inner side would then need `self.data.conversation_id = self.conversation_id` in `publish_to_context`. No test covers conversation id precedence yet.

This (and `tool_definitions`, `stop_sequences`) now returns a copy, so in-place changes are silently lost - it worked on main where these were plain lists. Keeping these `InferenceData` fields as `list` and returning them as-is would avoid it.

```python
def test_finish_reasons_append_is_recorded(self):
    with self.handler.inference("openai", request_model="m") as inv:
        inv.finish_reasons = []
        inv.finish_reasons.append("stop")
    (span,) = self.span_exporter.get_finished_spans()
    self.assertEqual(
        span.attributes.get(GenAI.GEN_AI_RESPONSE_FINISH_REASONS), ("stop",)
    )
```
